MY STORY ADVENTURE

My Beginning, Middle and End

Arrange your ideas into three connected parts.

Look, then try.

In the beginning, introduce the character and place. In the middle, show a problem and what the character tries. At the end, show what happens after their actions. Tell the story aloud and check that each part connects to the next.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps cut character cards. Keep small paper scraps away from younger children. You can draw, type or ask a grown-up to write your words.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Beginning

Draw who is here and where the story starts.

ACTIVITY 2

Middle

Draw the problem and what the character does.

ACTIVITY 3

End

Draw how the story finishes.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Sequencing and cause-and-effect help a story make sense. An ending can show a change, a discovery or a solved problem.
